facts.fact: AdImpact projects total political ad spending for the 2026 midterms will reach $10.8 billion, up 21% from the $8.9 billion spent in the 2022 cycle.
facts.quote: AdImpact projects total political ad spending will hit $10.8 billion, up 21% from the $8.9 billion spent during the 2022 cycle.

facts.fact: Broadcast television still commands the largest share of political ad budgets, at roughly 49% of total spend.
facts.quote: Broadcast television still commands the largest share of political ad budgets at roughly 49% of total spend.

facts.fact: AdImpact's Political Projections Report projects broadcast political spend to decline from $5.36 billion in 2024 to $5.28 billion in 2026.
facts.quote: Broadcast spend is projected to decline from $5.36 billion in 2024 to $5.28 billion in 2026, according to AdImpact's Political Projections Report.

facts.fact: According to eMarketer (2024), political CTV spending grew 600% between 2020 and 2024, from roughly $260 million to over $1.5 billion.
facts.quote: Political CTV spending grew 600% between 2020 and 2024, jumping from roughly $260 million to over $1.5 billion

facts.fact: AdImpact projects political CTV spend will reach $2.48 billion in 2026, a 20% increase over 2024 levels.
facts.quote: For 2026, AdImpact projects CTV political spend will reach $2.48 billion, a 20% increase over 2024 levels

facts.fact: CTV is the only media type that AdImpact expects to increase political ad spending compared to 2024.
facts.quote: CTV is the only media type that AdImpact expects to increase in spending compared to 2024.

facts.fact: More than 60% of U.S. households use streaming services as their primary TV source.
facts.quote: More than 60% of U.S. households now use streaming services as their primary TV source.

facts.fact: Traditional broadcast TV buys require minimum commitments of $50,000 or more, according to the page.
facts.quote: Traditional broadcast buys require minimum commitments of $50,000 or more

facts.fact: According to MadHive (2025), a school board candidate spending $2,000 on CTV can reach 80,000+ targeted impressions in their district.
facts.quote: A school board candidate spending $2,000 on CTV can reach 80,000+ targeted impressions in their district

facts.fact: Adwave states that the entry cost for TV advertising has dropped to as little as $30 a day through its platform.
facts.quote: The barrier to entry has dropped from tens of thousands of dollars to as little as $30 a day through platforms like Adwave.

facts.fact: The page states a traditional TV campaign ad production cost is $15,000 to $50,000 or more.
facts.quote: Total cost? $15,000 to $50,000 or more.

facts.fact: The page states a traditional TV campaign ad production timeline is four to six weeks minimum.
facts.quote: Four to six weeks, minimum.

facts.fact: Adwave states it can generate a broadcast-quality 30-second TV ad in about two minutes from a campaign website or social media page.
facts.quote: Adwave, for example, can generate a broadcast-quality 30-second TV ad in about two minutes

facts.fact: According to StackAdapt (2025), political data vendors L2, TargetSmart, and Data Trust deliver 50-70% voter file match rates for clean voter files on CTV.
facts.quote: improved their matching capabilities to deliver 50-70% match rates for clean voter files

facts.fact: The page says campaigns were seeing 30-40% voter file match rates on streaming households just two years before 2026.
facts.quote: the 30-40% match rates campaigns were seeing just two years ago.

facts.fact: In 2024, more than 60% of voters cast their ballots early or by mail.
facts.quote: In 2024, more than 60% of voters cast their ballots early or by mail.

facts.fact: The page states that statewide campaigns are allocating 15-25% of their total media budget to CTV this cycle.
facts.quote: Statewide campaigns are allocating 15-25% of their total media budget to CTV this cycle, which can mean millions of dollars for competitive Senate seats.

facts.fact: The page states that down-ballot races can run effective CTV campaigns for as little as a few hundred dollars.
facts.quote: Down-ballot races can run effective CTV campaigns for as little as a few hundred dollars.

facts.fact: The page states that a school board or city council candidate can run targeted CTV ads within their district for a few thousand dollars.
facts.quote: A school board or city council candidate can run targeted TV ads within their district for a few thousand dollars

facts.fact: The page states that the minimum spend on some CTV platforms starts at $50.
facts.quote: The minimum spend on some platforms starts at $50.

facts.fact: The page states that broadcast accounts for about 49% of political ad spend.
facts.quote: Broadcast accounts for about 49% of political ad spend and connected TV roughly 23%.

facts.fact: The page states that current voter file match rates on CTV run between 50-70% for well-maintained voter files.
facts.quote: Current match rates run between 50-70% for well-maintained voter files, meaning you can reach the majority of your target voters on their streaming devices.

facts.fact: The page states that campaigns deploying a programmatic TV response can get an ad on air in 24 to 48 hours, versus two-week broadcast insertion orders.
facts.quote: campaigns that can deploy a TV response in 24 to 48 hours have a serious advantage over those locked into two-week broadcast insertion orders.

facts.fact: The page states that with programmatic CTV a campaign can go from concept to live ad in under 24 hours.
facts.quote: With programmatic CTV, you can go from concept to live ad in under 24 hours.

facts.fact: The page states that with traditional broadcast, insertion orders and scheduling take days to weeks.
facts.quote: With traditional broadcast, you're looking at days to weeks for insertion orders and scheduling.

facts.fact: The page states that there is no federal law prohibiting the use of AI in political advertising, though some states are introducing disclosure requirements.
facts.quote: There's no federal law prohibiting the use of AI in political advertising, though some states are introducing disclosure requirements.

facts.fact: The page states that Texas saw widespread use of AI-generated political video during the 2026 primaries.
facts.quote: Texas, for example, saw widespread use of AI-generated political video during the 2026 primaries.
